newsitem.title: GERMANY: Rampant German bulls push DAX towards magic 3,000.
newsitem.headline: Rampant German bulls push DAX towards magic 3,000.

text.p: German technical analysts said on Monday they remain bullish on the DAX index's prospects for the remainder of the year and do not rule out the chance of the DAX hitting 3,000 points early next year.

The bullish outlook comes despite whisperings that if there is a harsh correction on Wall Street, where share prices have stormed higher recently, it could have serious consequences for the DAX, which often follows the United States when seeking direction.

"It looks like we could hit 3,000 points alright, and pretty soon. I like to use the options indicators -- normally at these levels people are bidding puts because they are scared of a crash and this gives protection on the downside," said Paul Lewis, technical trader at BNP in Frankfurt.
"What is happening is that everyone is just buying upside calls. It's like everyone is getting heady and disregarding the downside. People can only see upside," said Lewis.
The DAX index ended bourse trade in Frankfurt on Monday at a new record high at 2,799.19 points, up 35.50, just above an all-time high of 2,799.05 points which it hit on November 15.
In IBIS electronic trade in the afternoon, the DAX topped the 2,800-point level, trading as high as 2,805.75 points.

Ingo Mainert, chartist at Commerzbank, said: "The short-term indicators over the next one or two weeks show the DAX index has got the wind behind it, which indicates a definite upward potential to around 2,850 points."
Marcel Muessler, chartist at DG Bank in Frankfurt, is less bullish, but still believes the short-term trend is intact.
"We think the DAX in the short-term is going to hit around 2,820 points, say over the next week. But in the slightly longer term, in four weeks or so, we are more sceptical," said Muessler.
Volker Bien, technical analyst at BHF Bank in Frankfurt, says the DAX is in the last stage of an upward trend which has gone on since October of 1995.
"One of the main things driving market performance has been speculation of a cut in interest rates. Pessimism on a rate cut is no longer in the market, but it is not far away," said Bien.
Bien says that the German market does not yet look overbought.

Looking at share price direction indicators on the DAX-30, some 14 stocks showed upward trends, including Bayer and Veba, while eleven were neutral, including Lufthansa AG and Preussag AG, and only four had bearish trends, including Siemens and SAP.
German chartists are keeping a close eye on the Dow Jones Industrial index on Wall Street, which Bien says is overbought. At 1500 gmt the Dow was 13.42 points higher at 6485.18.
"There is always a risk in an extremely overbought situation. But, in Germany there are no sell signals yet and the stability of the upward trend is still intact," said Bien.
Ingo Mainert said: "For the year-end I believe the upwards trend could be sustained, but I would still be a little cautious on what the final outturn could be."
Chartists say that the recent Deutsche Telekom flotation has no impact on the classical chartists view of the DAX.

While the Telekom IPO does impact in terms of boosting volumes of trade, and strong volumes lead to strong stock performance, Mainert believes that in technical terms, the market weeds out the impact of volume on market fundamentals.
Muessler agrees and says that last week's consolidation was one that the charts had seen coming. "The consolidation which we had last week was totally normal in a technical sense," said Muessler.
Paul Lewis says that market players are acting as if the current upward movement is never going to end.
"Volatility is low. Any bearish corrections you see only last around two days, then turns around and hits a new high."
